chains.title: HNF4A binds the alt allele at a weak intronic element and alters FAM110B
chains.element: weak intronic sequence near a CA-H3K4me3 cCRE, not overlapping an ENCODE cCRE

links.claim: HNF4A is proposed to bind the alt T allele more strongly than the ref G allele at rs7001688. No QBiC-SELEX, MPRA, reporter, or allele-specific binding evidence is provided. E08 found no ENCODE HNF4A ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in HepG2, which weakens but does not exclude this chain because absence may also reflect no HNF4A experiment in that biosample. HNF4A was chosen as the only TF directly queried by a provided ChIP row; its QBiC coverage is not checked because no QBiC-SELEX evidence was supplied.

The variant is an intronic variant with no annotated regulatory feature and no ENCODE cCRE overlap; the nearest cCRE is a CA-H3K4me3 element 1544 bp away, so any regulatory element would be weak or indirect.

FAM110B is the nearest protein-coding gene at 420.6 kb, but distance alone does not establish regulation. There are no significant liver GTEx eQTLs for this variant, no Open Targets association between FAM110B and free cholesterol in large LDL, and the Europe PMC hit is not variant-specific.
Hep 3B2.1-7 is a hepatocyte-derived line, but the provided evidence contains no HNF4A expression, ChIP, or perturbation data in this cell type.

A change in FAM110B regulation could in principle influence LDL cholesterol, but there is no rs7001688-specific evidence. E06 is an indirect literature hit, E09 does not support a FAM110B free-cholesterol association, and E04/E05 report no variant-disease record.

predictions: HNF4A binds the alt T allele more strongly than ref G at rs7001688 in a hepatocyte context.
The region contacts FAM110B or another LDL-relevant gene in hepatocytes.
Modulating the element or FAM110B changes LDL cholesterol.
falsified_if: Allele-specific HNF4A binding assays in hepatocyte nuclear extract show no difference between alt T and ref G.
HNF4A ChIP-qPCR in Hep 3B2.1-7 shows no enrichment at the rs7001688 element.
No chromatin-contact or eQTL evidence links the region to FAM110B, or FAM110B perturbation does not affect LDL cholesterol.
